records.text: The term "Residential Property" shall refer to:
(a) Any property zoned by Central Authority to serve residential or housing-occupancy purposes.
The term "Property Owner" shall refer to:
(a) Any individual holding sole property rights to, or an active lease on, any residential property.
The term “Resident” shall refer to:
(a) Any authorized or whitelisted user of a Residential Property.

All Residential property, except Military Housing, shall remain outside the ownership, control, or management of the State of Mayflower. The State of Mayflower shall have no authority to acquire, lease, manage or allocate any Residential Property. The State shall make no effort to purchase or otherwise obtain Residential Property, and any such property currently held by the State, exempting Military Housing, shall be divested within a reasonable time as provided by law.
No individual shall own, either directly or through alternative accounts, more then one Residential Property.
(a) Violation of this section is a violation of 1 M.S.C. § 1404 "Unfair Housing Practices"
The State of Mayflower shall be the Property Owner of all unoccupied Military Housing.
(a) Any active serviceman of the Mayflower National Guard may submit a request to the Adjutant General, or his designee, to purchase a Military Home for an agreed upon amount of time.
(b) The Adjutant General of the Mayflower National Guard, or his designee, shall make an effort to house any unhoused active serviceman in unoccupied Military Housing.
No person shall operate a business without a proper license from the Department of State.
No business entity shall operate in a manner inconsistent with regulations promulgated by the Secretary of State in accordance with this Section.

(a) Regulations applied to any business entity promulgated by the Secretary of State in accordance with this act shall be created and enforced in a manner that ensures they do not unduly obstruct or excessively restrict business operations, thereby maintaining a balance between regulatory compliance and the ability of businesses to operate effectively and efficiently.
The Secretary of State shall ensure that all documents and information prerequisite is provided on the registration.
There shall be a form, known as the “Application for Articles of Organization” that shall be publicly available by the Department of State.
The Secretary of State shall refuse to file an articles of incorporation if it does not meet the following standards:
(a) The name of the corporation is clearly typed and designated as such.
(b) It must contain an initial appointment of the board of directors.
(c) It must contain the number of authorized shares and who the shares are distributed to.
(d) The name of the incorporator is clearly typed and designated as such.
(e) It must contain an attached set of bylaws which shall dictate the appointment of the board of directors and the further apportionment or sale of shares.
The Secretary of State shall refuse to file an articles of general partnership if it does not meet the following standards:
(a) The name of the general partnership is clearly typed and designated as such.
(b) The initial partners.
(c) Authorization for a majority of partners to modify the general partnership including the admittance or expulsion of partners.
(d) The designation and appointment of a managing partner.

The Secretary of State shall examine trademark applications to ensure compliance with the requirements set forth in this act, in addition to any additional requirements that the Secretary of State deems necessary.
Upon determination that a trademark meets all necessary criteria, including distinctiveness and non-conflict with any existing trademarks, the Secretary of State shall approve the registration.

Once a trademark has been registered with the Department of State with the approval of the Secretary of State, no other person or business entity may use the trademark unless permitted by the person or business entity who owns the rights to the trademark.
The Secretary of State is required to maintain a public registry of trademarks in use. This registry shall include information regarding:
(a) The registered trademark;
(b) The owner; and
(c) The goods or services associated with each trademark.
Owners of registered trademarks shall be required to renew their trademark registrations periodically, as prescribed by the Secretary of State.
If a registered trademark is revoked for any reason, including but not limited to non-renewal or infringement, the public shall once again be permitted to use the trademark.
No person or business entity shall use a trademark without the explicit permission, in writing, from the registered owner of the trademark.

(a) Violation of this section shall be a civil tort referred to as as "Civil Trademark Infringement" punishable by declaratory judgement removing the use of said trademarks and punitive damages up to $3000.

Any person or business entity who contravenes any provision of this Section shall, in addition to any other penalty or punishment to which the person or business entity may be liable to, be subject to the following penalties upon conviction:
(a) In the case of a business entity, a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars.
(b) In the case of an individual, the crime of “Unlawful Operation of a Business”, or a fine not exceeding two thousand dollars, or both.

records.text: CIVIL PENALTY. Any person, firm, corporation, association, or entity, or any agent or employee of the foregoing, who is willfully using, or has willfully used, a method, act, or practice declared unlawful, or who is willfully violating any of the rules of the department adopted under this part, is liable for a civil penalty of not more than $10,000 for each such violation. Willful violations occur when the person knew or should have known that his or her conduct was unfair or deceptive or prohibited by rule. This civil penalty may be recovered in any action brought under this part by the enforcing authority; or the enforcing authority may terminate any investigation or action upon agreement by the person, firm, corporation, association, or entity, or the agent or employee of the foregoing, to pay a stipulated civil penalty. The department or the court may waive any such civil penalty if the person, firm, corporation, association, or entity, or the agent or employee of the foregoing, has previously made full restitution or reimbursement or has paid actual damages to the consumers or governmental entities who have been injured by the unlawful act or practice or rule violation. If civil penalties are assessed in any litigation, the enforcing authority is entitled to reasonable attorney’s fees and costs.

records.text: The term “Racketeering Activity” shall refer to:

(a) Any act or threat involving murder, kidnapping, battery, use of deadly weapons in the commission of an offense, gambling, arson, robbery, bribery, extortion, dealing in obscene matter, bribery, embezzlement, fraud, obstruction of justice, obstruction of criminal investigations, tampering with a witness, victim, or informant; monetary transactions of unlawfully gained property, murder for hire, or weapons trafficking.
The term "enterprise” shall include:

(a) For the purposes of this Chapter, "enterprise" means any person, sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation, or other legal entity; or any association, or group of persons associated in fact although not a legal entity; and it includes illicit as well as licit enterprises and governmental as well as other entities.
The term “person” shall include:
(a) Any individual or entity capable of holding a legal or beneficial interest in property.
The term "pattering of racketeering activity" shall refer to:

(a) At least two acts of racketeering activity, one of which occurred after the effective date of this chapter and the last of which occurred within six months (excluding any period of imprisonment) after the commission of a prior act of racketeering activity.

It shall be unlawful for any person through a pattern of racketeering activity or through collection of an unlawful debt to acquire or maintain, directly or indirectly, any interest in or control of any enterprise which is engaged in, or the activities of which affect commerce.

It shall be unlawful for any person employed by or associated with any enterprise engaged in, or the activities of which affect commerce, to conduct or participate, directly or indirectly, in the conduct of such enterprise’s affairs through a pattern of racketeering activity or collection of unlawful debt.
It shall be unlawful for any person to conspire to violate any of the provisions of this subsection.
(a) Whoever violates any provision of this subsection is guilty of racketeering which shall be a felony punishable by up to 35 minutes in jail.

In proceedings of racketeering, the Attorney General may petition the court to dissolve a business, and force the immediate sale of their properties, and divide outstanding debts amongst its liable persons.

The Attorney General or other authorized attorney for the government may petition the State District Court in the relevant judicial district for the seizure of any assets, securities, assets, or money derived from or used in racketeering activity.

The Attorney General may sue on behalf of the State any organization engaged in a pattern of racketeering activity, or any individual engaged in a pattern of racketeering activity, to recoup treble damages of any offenses committed against the State or any of its officers.

Whoever is convicted of 1 M.S.C. § 5202 “Racketeering” or 1 M.S.C. § 5203 “Racketeering conspiracy” shall forfeit to the State of Mayflower any (1) interest in; (2) security of; (3) claim against, or; (4) property or contractual right of any kind affording a source of influence over any enterprise which the person has established, operated, controlled, conducted, or participated in the conduct of, in violation of § 5202 or § 5203, and any property constituting, or derived from, any proceeds which the person obtained, directly or indirectly, from racketeering activity.

Any person injured in his business or property by reason of a violation of this subchapter may sue in the District Court and shall recover threefold the damages he sustains and the cost of the suit, including a reasonable attorney’s fee.
The term “Criminal Street Gang” shall refer to:

(a) Any ongoing organization, association, or group of three or more persons, whether formal or informal, having as one of its primary activities the commission of one or more criminal acts or racketeering activity, whose members individually or collectively engage in or have engaged in a pattern of criminal or racketeering activity; or,

(b) Any organization association, or group of three or more persons, whether formal or informal, declared by the Governor, Attorney General, or the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation Director by public proclamation, as a criminal street gang; or
(c) Any organization, association, or group of two or more persons participating in criminal or racketeering activity in conjunction with a criminal street gang.
The term “person” or "player" shall be used interchangably and shall refer to:
(a) any individual or entity capable of holding a legal or beneficial interest in property;

A person shall be guilty of coercing, inducing, or soliciting membership in a criminal street gang if the person knowingly causes, enables, encourages, recruits, or solicits another person to become a member of a criminal street gang which, as a condition of initiation, admission, membership, or continued membership, requires the commission of any conduct which constitutes an offense punishable as a felony or misdemeanor. This charge shall be a felony punishable by up to 45 minutes of incarceration.

A person shall be guilty of engaging in organized criminal activity if, with the intent to establish, maintain, or participate in a combination or in the profits of a combination or as a member of a criminal street gang, the person commits or conspires to commit one or more of the following: murder, arson, aggravated robbery, robbery, burglary, theft, aggravated kidnapping, kidnapping, aggravated assault, forgery, deadly conduct, assault, burglary of a motor vehicle, unauthorized use of a motor vehicle, or any racketeering activity, or any felony. This charge shall be a felony punishable by up to 50 minutes of incarceration.

A person shall be guilty of directing the activities of a criminal street gang if the person, as part of the identifiable leadership of a of a criminal street gang, knowingly finances, directs, or supervises the commission of, or a conspiracy to commit one or more of the following: murder, arson, aggravated robbery, robbery, burglary, theft, aggravated kidnapping, kidnapping, aggravated assault, forgery, deadly conduct, assault, burglary of a motor vehicle, unauthorized use of a motor vehicle, or any racketeering activity, or any felony. This charge shall be a felony punishable by up to 50 minutes of incarceration.

Any law enforcement officer with an active burn permit shall be further authorized to execute a controlled burn on vehicle used by a criminal street gang in conjunction with criminal activity, or purchased as a result of proceeds derived from the unlawful activities of a criminal street gang. Furthermore, any Guardsman may conduct a controlled burn on any vehicle used by a criminal street gang to effectuate an attack on any Military Exclusion Zone.
(a) This provision shall only take effect if authorized by the Governor, Attorney General, or the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation Director for a specific timeframe or organization.

The Mayflower Bureau of Investigation Director or their designee shall have the responsibility to maintain a public listing of all recognised criminal street gangs, as defined under 4 M.S.C. 2 § 2101 and its subsections, for which there will be a review every 30 days of their designated status to determine if they are an active and current threat to state security and safety.
The term “classified information” shall refer to:
(a) Information regulated by the provisions of this act to be confidential; specifically designated by a State Government Agency for limited or restricted dissemination or distribution.
The term “department head” shall refer to:
(a) The first-in-command of an agency under the executive cabinet, or the head of a law enforcement agency within the State of Mayflower.
The term “security clearance” shall refer to:
(a) An official authorization to access classified information designated by the provisions of this act.
Information may be classified at one of the following four levels upon meeting its’ criteria:

(a) “Top Secret” shall be applied to information, the unauthorized disclosure of which reasonably could be expected to cause exceptionally grave damage to the state security or impede ongoing criminal investigations or judicial processes that the original classification authority is able to identify or describe.

(b) “Secret” shall be applied to information, the unauthorized disclosure of which reasonably could be expected to cause serious damage to the state security or impede ongoing criminal investigations or judicial processes.

(c) “Confidential” shall be applied to information, the unauthorized disclosure of which reasonably could be expected to cause damage to the state security or impede ongoing criminal investigations or judicial processes.
(d) "O" shall be applied to information of the highest sensitivity, accessible only to the Governor, the State Intelligence Director, and individuals explicitly cleared by both.

At the time of original classification, the following shall appear on the face of each classified document, or shall be applied to other classified media in an appropriate manner in order to be considered classified information:
One of the three classification levels defined in Subchapter II of this Chapter.
The date of classification
The username of the individual with classification authority.
The date that is no more than 1 year from the date of original classification pursuant to paragraph (a)(ii) of this section.
Classified material shall remain protected under its classification for no more than one (1) year.

(a) An original classification authority may extend the duration of classification, change the level of classification, or reclassify specific information only when the standards and procedures for classifying information under this act, and by authority of the Governor to classify information.
The Governor shall have the authority to issue orders on the handling, procedure, criteria, or any otherwise necessary provisions for classifying information.

Categories for the classification of information must serve a reasonable and objective purpose of securing information that if disclosed, would be either damaging to state security, public safety, criminal investigations, defense, or life-threatening harm to individuals.
The authority to classify information originally shall only be exercised by:
The Governor of the State of Mayflower, in the performance of executive duties, the Lieutenant Governor;
Department heads and officials designated by the Governor through executive decree.
State government officials delegated this authority by paragraph (b) of this section.
State government officials delegated this authority by paragraph (b) of this section.

(i) Material which is classified by the Adjutant General, his deputy or any authorised officials thereof to which he delegates his authority may be subject to review, reclassification or reversal of their original classification status by the Director of State Intelligence which must be provided in writing. No material of the same (or inherently similar) nature may be reclassified without the approval of the Director of State Intelligence or the Governor in writing so as to subvert this clause.

“Confidential,” “Secret” or “Top Secret” may be delegated by the Governor; in the performance of executive duties, the Lieutenant Governor; or a department head or official designated pursuant to paragraph 1401 of this section; or a subordinate designated by a department head to classify information.

All Commissioned Officers of the Mayflower National Guard shall be issued the Security Clearance of Secret as defined by 4 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(b) upon completing Officer Candidate School or its equivalent.

All Senators appointed to the Senate Standing Committee on State Security, who have been vetted by the Office of State Intelligence, shall be issued a "Top Secret" security clearance, as defined in 4 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(a).
All Senators appointed to the Senate Standing Committee on State Security shall be vetted for the following criteria:

(a) Whether the Senator has alternate accounts, registered and unregistered, and reasonably determine if said accounts are connected to declared Street Gangs, Criminal Organizations, or Terrorist Organizations.
(b) Whether the Senator's inventory is open.
(c) Whether the Senator is involved with a street gang, criminal or terrorist organization which has been declared by the Attorney General.

(d) Whether the Senator has a criminal conviction of: any offence under Title 1, Subtitle 1, Chapter 1; Title 1, Subtitle 1, Chapter 6; Title 1, Subtitle 1, Chapter 9; Title 1, Subtitle 5, Chapter 1; Title 1, Subtitle 5, Chapter 2; any form of misconduct; 1 M.S.C. § 1201 "Concealing/destroying evidence;" 1 M.S.C. § 1401 "Unauthorized Disclosure of Trade Secrets;" or 1 M.S.C. § 1410 "Corporate Espionage."

The Office of State Intelligence shall have the sole authority to issue, revoke, and regulate security clearances within the State of Mayflower. The Director of State Intelligence may designate officials who hold the authority to issue, revoke, and regulate security clearances.

(a) This power shall not extend to Commissioned Officers of the Mayflower National Guard, although the Director of State Intelligence shall retain the power to petition in writing, to the Governor, for the suspension, revocation or regulation of security clearances for members of Commissioned Officers of the Mayflower National Guard.

(b) This power shall not extend to vetted Senators of the Senate Standing Committee on State Security, although the Director of State Intelligence shall retain the power to petition in writing, to the Governor, for the temporary suspension of members of the Senate Standing Committee on State Security for such actions regarding committee members, providing a detailed justification based on conflicts of interests or misconduct.
No individual may view classified information without a security clearance of the same classification level.

records.text: Every department or railroad company that employs at least one peace officer is required to establish an internal investigation unit that is staffed with at least one peace officer who shall not be in any other division or department office. The duties of this unit shall include, but are not limited to, the following:
(a) Primary duties include, but are not limited to:
(i) ensuring employed peace officers are compliant with department policies;
(ii) ensuring employed peace officers are compliant with regulations issued by the Attorney General;
(iii) maintaining confidentiality where appropriate;
(iv) conducting impartial investigations regarding contraventions of department policies, this act, and any regulations prescribed under this act; and
(v) recommend re-education training or disciplinary measures to the department head.
(b) From time to time, issue a publicly accessible document or message regarding disciplinary measures taken within the respective department since the last publication.
(c) Forward the result and any relevant documentation to the Attorney General upon conclusion of any investigation.
(d) Ensure that an accessible method for reporting police misconduct is available to the public.
In the event that a complaint regarding a department head is received, the internal investigation unit shall notify the Attorney General upon receiving the complaint.
The department head of a law enforcement agency shall have the authority to:
(a) establish or amend written procedures regarding the administration of their respective department;
(b) approve re-education training or disciplinary measures suggested by their respective department’s internal investigation unit; and

(c) delegate in writing any powers and duties in this act, or its regulations, to a member or office of their respective department, subject to any limitations, conditions or requirements set out in the delegation.
The department head of a law enforcement agency is responsible for:
(a) ensuring department policies and procedures are in compliance with all applicable laws and regulations;
(b) overseeing and managing all activities of their respective department;
(c) in writing, authorizing police operations in their respective department; and
(d) approving all offers of employment of their respective department.
This chapter applies to postal inspectors, peace officers employed and acting under a port authority, and any other law enforcement agency not established directly by the State or by State law.

records.text: When it is reasonably safe for a peace officer, every peace officer upon request from any person is required to:
(a) show their identification card;
(b) state the department they are acting in the capacity of; and
(c) if applicable, state their callsign.
A peace officer is not required to identify themselves if:
(a) it is not reasonably safe for the peace officer;
(b) the peace officer is operating an emergency service vehicle;
(c) the peace officer has already identified themselves to the same person within the last sixty (60) minutes;
(d) the peace officer has declared themselves out of service; or
(e) the peace officer is engaged in or participating in an authorized police operation where the act of providing identification would compromise the objective(s) of the operation.

The Attorney General may make regulations towards any law enforcement agency, personnel, or leadership, in the interest of ensuring that the law is enforced properly, ethical pratices are maintained, and the safety of the State is prioritized.
(a) Any public employee who violates a published law enforcement memorandum unintentionally as a result of negligence shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1304 "Misconduct."
(b) Any public employee who violates a published law enforcement memorandum knowingly or intentionally shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1303 "Gross Misconduct."
(c) All departments who employ law enforcement officers shall develop policies governing requirements for compliance with published memorandums, and punishment for disobedience from employees.

(d) The Attorney General may, at their discretion, may choose to outline certain instances in which there is individual liability of an officer rather than official liability in instances of failure to execute such memorandums.
The Attorney General shall notify the head of any department effected of any creation, amendment, revocation, or any other alteration of a regulation prescribed under this subchapter.

The provisions of any regulation prescribed by the Attorney General under this subchapter shall be interpreted as being in addition to, and not in derogation or restriction of, any power, jurisdiction or authority that may be exercised under this Chapter, the Constitution, or any other Chapter.

Any person who contravenes 4 M.S.C. 5 §§ 1302-1309, 4 M.S.C. 5 § 1601, 4 M.S.C. 5 § 2204, or 4 M.S.C. 5 § 2401 is guilty of an offense and is liable on conviction, in addition to any other penalty or punishment to which the person may be guilty, is guilty:
(a) in the case of an unintentional action that does not result in a threat to life, to misconduct;
(b) in the case of an intentional action that does not result in a threat to life, to gross misconduct; or
(c) in the case of an action that results in a threat to life, to felony misconduct.
The Governor may, for a renewable period of up to one hundred twenty (120) days, appoint a person as a peace officer for the purposes of this act, subject to the following conditions and limitations:
(a) The person is a certified and commissioned peace officer in another State within the Union of Columbia.

(i) Persons who meet this requirement and are appointed under this subchapter shall be considered certified for the purposes of Article VIII, Section 3 of the Constitution for the duration of their appointment.
(b) The person shall have the same responsibilities as any other peace officer normally employed directly or indirectly by a law enforcement agency in the State of Mayflower.
(c) Any other conditions, limitations, stipuplations, or requirements listed in the appointment.

The Colonel of the Mayflower State Police shall ensure that persons appointed as peace officers under this subchapter are provided access to equipment and facilities normally given to peace officers employed under the Mayflower State Police.
(a) The internal investigation unit of the Mayflower State Police shall handle all complaints regarding persons appointed as peace officers under this subchapter.

In this Subtitle, any reference to a pronoun shall be interpreted to include all respective pronouns, regardless of gender. Terms such as 'he,' 'him,' or 'his' shall be deemed to include 'she,' 'her,' 'hers,' 'they,' 'them,' 'theirs,' or any other pronoun as applicable. This inclusive interpretation applies to all provisions, ensuring gender neutrality and inclusivity throughout this act.
This chapter may be cited as the "Police Detainment Act."

records.text: A traffic stop may not last more than twelve (12) minutes.
(a) After twelve (12) minutes have passed since the commencement of the traffic stop, all charges on the operator of the motor vehicle shall be void.
An interrogation may not last for more than forty-five (45) minutes.

(a) After forty-five (45) minutes have passed since the start of the interrogation, or the peace officer conducting the interrogation has terminated the interrogation, the peace officer has an additional fifteen (15) minutes to charge the detained person with a crime.

(b) If the peace officer conducting the interrogation takes longer than forty-five (45) minutes, no more questions may be asked and the interrogation shall conclude. The detained person shall be free to leave.

(i) This does not apply if the detained person willingly continues the interrogation. If the detained person willingly continues the interrogation, they shall be free to leave at any time unless the peace officer conducting the interrogation decides to charge the detained person with a crime, to which 4 M.S.C. 5 § 3202(a) shall take effect.

(c) Proceeding the termination of the interrogation, if the peace officer that was conducting the interrogation takes longer than the additional fifteen (15) minutes allocated to book the detained person, the charges against the detained person shall be void.

Any other detainment in any other setting shall not exceed more than twelve (12) minutes. For the purposes of this code, the detainment commences whenever the peace officer verbally informs the person that they are being detained, or places handcuffs on the person, or both.
(a) After twelve (12) minutes have passed since the commencement of the detainment, all charges against the detained person shall be void.

If a detained person requests a bar certified attorney, any timer relevant to the detainment shall be halted. Upon the arrival of the detained person's bar certified attorney, or the detained person has informed the peace officer that their bar ceritifed attorney is no longer coming, the relevant detainment timer shall resume.
Notwithstanding 4 M.S.C. 5 § 3202, an interrogation may last for up ninety (90) minutes provided the following conditions are met:
(a) the peace officer conducting the interrogation is employed by the same department as the detained person;

(b) the peace officer is a higher rank than the detained person in the department, or the peace officer is a member of that department's internal investigation unit formed under 4 M.S.C. 5 § 1701; and
(c) the detained person has not been interrogated within the past twelve (12) hours under 4 M.S.C. 5 § 3202.

(a) After ninety (90) minutes have passed since the start of the interrogation, or the peace officer conducting the interrogation has terminated the interrogation, the peace officer has an additional fifteen (15) minutes to charge the detained person with a crime. After the additional fifteen (15) minutes, all charges against the detained person shall be void.

If any detained person requests a supervisor, any relevant detainment timer shall halt, provided that the peace officer detaining the detained person is not a supervisor themselves. If the peace officer is considered a supervisor, they may act in the capacity of a supervisor for the purposes of the request.

records.text: The term “firearm” shall refer to the definition prescribed by 4 M.S.C. 5 § 6101(a).
“Dispense” shall be defined as:

(a) Any firearm which is made available to a person through an equipment dispenser device of which the ability to dispense such a firearm is made available through employment or otherwise similar status within an authorized organization. This definition shall include though not be limited to firearms provided by government departments, agencies, or otherwise authorized authorities.
The term “automatic firearm” shall be defined as;
(a) Any self-loading firearm capable of continuously firing projectiles when the trigger mechanism is activated.
(b) Any self-loading firearm capable of firing multiple projectiles per a single activation of the trigger mechanism.
The term “firearm modification” shall be defined as;

(a) Any component, attachment, or accessory designed or used to alter or enhance the functionality, performance, or characteristics of a weapon from its original manufactured state, including but not limited to devices affecting rate of fire, accuracy, caliber, or concealability.
(b) Any physical modification of the mechanical or external components of a firearm from its original manufactured state.
(c) This definition shall include though not be limited to removable devices such as weapon optics, barrel attachments, and otherwise similar devices.
The term “Licensed Vendor” shall be defined as;
(a) Any individual person(s), organizations, private institutions or otherwise stores licensed to operate and participate in the trade and or sale of firearms,
The term “Illicit Vendor” shall be defined as;
(a) Any individual person(s), organizations, private institutions or otherwise stores which participate in the trade and or sale of firearms without being licensed to do so.
No individual shall be permitted to have within their possession a firearm in any capacity without having within their name a valid state issued firearms license.
(a) Any individual found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4401 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6102 Unlicensed Possession of a Firearm.

No individual shall be permitted to have within their possession a restricted-grade firearm in any capacity unless they are employed by, or otherwise affiliated with, an organization able to dispense, or are authorized by law to grant designated individuals permission to carry, such firearms as part of their official duties, and the organization has authorized the individual to carry such a firearm in the performance of their duties or otherwise lawful authorized environments.
(a) An individual authorized under 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4402 to carry a dispense firearm must be in compliance with all provisions of legislation related to the possession of such a firearm.

(b) A peace officer shall be temporarily authorized to possess a restricted-grade firearm which they are not otherwise authorized to possess under 4 M.S.C. § 4402 for the purposes of seizure and destruction, but must place the restricted-grade firearm in the trunk of a department-issued vehicle as soon as is practicably possible.
No individual shall be permitted to have within their possession any firearm sourced from an illicit vendor.
(a) Any individual found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4404 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6102 Unlicensed Possession of a Firearm.
A prospective Licensed Vendor must apply for a Firearm Trade Permit from the Commerce Office.
(a) The Commerce Office may create requirements to obtain a Firearm Trade Permit.
A Firearm Trade Permit may only be given out with the consent of the Lee County Sheriff.
The Commerce Office shall maintain a database of all active Firearm Trade Permits.
No individual or organization that fails to meet the definition of a Licensed Vendor shall engage in the trade of firearms of any designation.
(a) Any individual or organization found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4501 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6201 Unlawful dealing of a firearm.

A Licensed Vendor shall be permitted only to participate in the trade and or sale of firearms of which the possession of is not regulated by the provisions of this act (not including 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4301), provided both parties participating in the trade have within their name a valid state firearms license.
(a) Any individual or organization found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4502 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6201 Unlawful dealing of a firearm.

Any individual in possession of a firearm with a modification made to, affixed to, or installed on that serves any of the following purposes shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 6102: Unlicensed Possession of a Firearm;
(a) Barrel attachments or other modifications which suppress or otherwise silence the audible noise generated by the process of discharging a projectile.
(b) Modification to reduce the length of a firearms barrel to be less than three (3) studs in length, or to reduce the length of the firearm entirely to be less than six (6) studs.
No individual shall be permitted to have within their possession any form of firearm ammunition in any capacity without having within their name a valid state issued firearms license.
(a) Any individual found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4701 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6104 Unlicensed Possession of ammunition.
No individual shall be permitted to have within their possession any form of firearm ammunition sourced from an illicit vendor.
(a) Any individual found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4702 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6104 Unlicensed Possession of ammunition.

No individual who is not defined as a peace officer or active member of the armed services shall be permitted to have within their possession any form of firearm magazine which physically can service a surplus of twenty (20) rounds of ammunition.
(a) Any individual found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4703 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6103 Unauthorized possession of a high-capacity magazine.

No individual or organization that fails to meet the definition of a Licensed Vendor shall engage in the trade of ammunition in excess of more than five (5) magazines, boxes, clips or otherwise devices within a twelve (12) hour period.
(a) Any individual found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4704 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6104 Unlicensed Possession of ammunition.

(b) Any individual or organization which partakes in the trade of ammunition when both parties do not have within their possession a valid state firearms license shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6202 Unlawful dealing of ammunition.

A Licensed Vendor shall be permitted only to participate in the trade and or sale of ammunition of which the possession of is not regulated by the provisions of this act (not including 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4201), provided both parties participating in the trade have within their name a valid state firearms license.
(a) Any individual found to be in contravention of 4 M.S.C. 5 § 4705 shall be guilty 1 M.S.C. § 6202 Unlawful dealing of ammunition.
A state issued firearm license shall only be issued to individuals who are lawful residents of the State of Mayflower.
A state issued firearm license shall be revoked by law enforcement officers if the holder of the license:
(a) Commits a crime involving the use, carriage, discharge or possession of a firearm, ammunition, or non-civilian equipment.
(b) Is a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization.
(c) Is deported from the State, or otherwise loses their residency.
A state issued firearm license shall be revoked for only 24 hours, unless otherwise specified by a court order.
Law enforcement officers who revoke a state issued firearm license must appropriately log the revocation in a manner deemed appropriate by the Attorney General.
If an individual with a firearm license is found in violation of a crime that would result in their firearm license being revoked, then any firearm or ammunition in their possession may be seized.

All Government run departments and agencies under the executive branch(es) of government, including law enforcement agencies, within the state shall be obligated to create and publish a public database, that is easily accessible within a separate public documents or similarly titled channel within a department’s communication server, and has:
(a) a registry of employees and each employees:
(i) assigned unit/division;
(ii) current position;
(iii) rank;
(iv) callsign/badge number; and
(v) complete disciplinary history;
(b) a code of conduct with all punitive titles as defined by 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1003;
(c) a list of all discharges; and
(d) a list of all administrative actions.
Any department or agency head who fails to comply with this subchapter shall be liable for Gross Misconduct and shall be prosecuted by the Department of Justice.
A “Whistleblower” shall be defined as a person who discloses information protected by a court order, nondisclosure agreement, state secrecy, or otherwise protected as permitted under this subchapter.

WHISTLEBLOWER PROTECTION. A whistleblower shall have the right to disclose information that is not otherwise publicly accessible, without threat of legal action, retaliation, or penalty, if the disclosure is made in good faith and based on a reasonable belief that one or more of the following conditions exists:
(a) A reasonable threat to public security or safety.
(b) Abuse by an authority.
(c) Violation of any law or regulation.
(d) Gross mismanagement.
A State Agency may not retaliate against a whistleblower in a manner including but not limited to:
(a) Threats.
(b) Demotion.
(c) Termination of employment.
(d) Legal action.
A whistleblower shall be guaranteed a return to their position of employment should a State Agency be found to have retaliated against the whistleblower.
A whistleblower's identity shall be kept confidential unless they consent to be revealed.
The protections of this subchapter shall apply regardless of whether the allegation is later substantiated, provided the whistleblower had a reasonable and honest belief at the time of disclosure.
No State Agency or official may require, as a condition of employment, any waiver or nondisclosure agreement that would limit or prohibit disclosures protected under this subchapter.

WHISTLEBLOWER PROTECTION; ENFORCEMENT. Should a whistleblower be retaliated against by a State Agency for the action of whistleblowing, then the State Agency will be liable to be subjected to various civil penalties as outlined by the Mayflower Tort Claims Act.
Any player that retaliates against a whistleblower for personal gain shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1302 “Felony Misconduct”.
Any player that retaliates against a whistleblower shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1303 “Gross Misconduct."
Any peace officer who has knowledge of retaliation but fails to report it shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 4202 “Attempt to commit a crime."
DEFINITIONS. A “State Agency” shall be defined as any government agency or department in the executive, legislative or judicial branch of the government.
A “FOIA requester” shall be defined as a resident of the State of Mayflower who is requesting materials as permitted under this act.
A “FOIA officer” or “Freedom of Information Access Officer” shall be defined as an employee of a State Agency who is responsible for responding to FOIA requests.
A “Whistleblower” shall be defined as a person who discloses information protected by a court order, nondisclosure agreement or state secrecy as permitted under this act.
FREEDOM OF INFORMATION REQUESTS. Residents of the State of Mayflower have the right to request access to any record or information of a state agency, except where it is exempted as:

(a) The file(s) are classified for the defence, security, or foreign policy of the state and the file(s) as a whole fall under a classification level as designated under Title 4, Chapter I, Subchapter II of the Mayflower State Code.
(b) The file(s) are trade secrets or confidential business records.
(c) The file(s) relate to personnel records, unless it is the personnel records of the FOIA requester.

(d) The file(s) relates to law enforcement records, operations, processes, information, techniques, or would deprive a person of the right to a fair trial, or reveal the identity of a confidential informant.
(e) The file(s) relate to a State Agency academy or education.
(f) The file(s) relate to foreign or domestic intelligence or counterintelligence.
(g) The file(s) relate to the identity of a witness.
If the file(s) that a FOIA requester is asking for does not exist, then the FOIA officer must notify the FOIA requester of such.
If the request submitted by the FOIA requester is too broad, then the FOIA officer may deny the request and notify the FOIA requester of such.

If file(s) requested by a FOIA requester contains lines, pages, portions, or media which is deemed to fall under a classification level as designated under Title 4, Chapter I, Subchapter II of the Mayflower State Code, then the FOIA officer must make a copy of the original file(s) and redact such information from the file(s), but not delete it, before submitting it to the FOIA requester where the reason for the redactions are clearly labelled.
When submitting a FOIA, the FOIA requester must ensure that they:
(a) Describe in as much detail as possible the file(s) being requested.
(b) Inform the State Agency of the purpose of the request.
Every state agency shall employ a Freedom of Information Access Officer.
(a) This employee may be a civilian employee.
(b) The department head of a State Agency shall be assumed to be the FOIA Officer should the role not be delegated to another individual.
The FOIA Officer shall be responsible for:
(a) Handling FOIA requests.
(b) Managing and publishing a publicly accessible FOIA request form for the state agency for which they are employed.
(c) Managing a database that contains all file(s) related to the State Agency for which they are employed.
(d) Further redacting file(s) which are requested by a FOIA requester so that it may be publicly viewable.
The Freedom of Information Access Officer must respond to a FOIA Requester within 4 days of a FOIA request and:
(a) Provide the FOIA requester with the requested information.
(b) Partially provide the FOIA requester with the requested information, and inform the FOIA requester that the remainder of the request is exempted from the request, and cite the exemption.
(c) Inform the FOIA requester that their request will not be fulfilled due to falling under an exemption, and cite the exemption.
(d) Inform the FOIA requester that the Freedom of Information Access Officer requires additional time to fulfil the request, and that it will be fulfilled within the next 3 days.

(e) Request that the FOIA requester further clarifies their request. Should this need arise, the time requirement shall reset upon the FOIA requester clarifying their request, or shall be denied should the FOIA requester not respond within 24 hours of the Freedom of Information Access Officer requesting the clarification.

FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ACCESS. Should a State Agency fail to respond to a FOIA request, then the FOIA requester may petition a court to order the release of the file(s) within 24 hours, unless the file(s) fall under an aforementioned exemption.
ENFORCEMENT. Should a State Agency fail to respond to a court order, then the FOIA officer shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1304 “Misconduct”.

records.text: All law enforcement officers and Special Forces members who wish to carry out Burns must hold an active Burn Permit Certification, issued by the Controlled Burns & Explosives Office.

All law enforcement officers and Special Forces members without prior history of misconduct relating to Burns shall be eligible for a Burn Permit, and must achieve 85% (eighty five percent) or higher in the Burn Permit Assessment.

Controlled Burns & Explosives Office shall be obliged to open the Burn Permit Assessment indefinitely throughout all times of the year and regularly mark responses, releasing results and issuing Burn Permits every 2 (two) weeks or less.

The Controlled Burns & Explosives Office shall be obliged to release and regularly review a forum for members of the public to report misconduct pertaining to Burns, and shall be obliged to investigate each report to the fullest.

The Controlled Burns & Explosives Office shall reserve the right to blacklist, revoke or suspend Burn Permits from law enforcement officers found to be in violation of the Burn Guide and other regulations clearly set by the Controlled Burns & Explosives Office. The severity of the administrative action shall be based on the severity of the misconduct committed, however shall be to the discretion of the Controlled Burns & Explosives Office.

Whilst the Controlled Burns & Explosives Office shall be entrusted with releasing safety regulations through their Burn Guide, the following details must be met for a vehicle to be eligible to be burnt;
(a) Vehicle contains 10 (ten) or more items defined by State Laws to be illegal for possession by the registered vehicle owner.

A vehicle with less than 10 (ten) items illegal for possession by the registered vehicle owner may be burnt by law enforcement officers only if the vehicle is a special vehicle registered to be owned by a member of a criminal street gang or terrorist organization, as declared by the Attorney General.
“Special Forces” shall be defined as the 19th Special Forces Group (AIRBORNE), an operational unit of the Mayflower National Guard, permanently stationed at Fort Standish.

“Special Forces member” shall be defined as an enlisted soldier or commissioned officer who is a duly assigned and qualified member of the 19th Special Forces Group (AIRBORNE) of the Mayflower National Guard, having completed all requisite training, certification, and assignment criteria as established by applicable military regulations and directives.
Any item within this section shall be known as Prohibited Goods.
It shall be illegal for an individual to be in unlawful possession of any goods listed in this subchapter.
The following items shall collectively be known as ‘Prohibited Goods, Class I’, or any other similar name
(a) Items, kits, or modifications tools that can be used to modify an automatic firearm;
(b) Items, kits, or modification tools which can cause a firearm that is not an automatic firearm to become so;
(c) Law enforcement exclusive equipment.
The following items shall collectively be known as ‘Prohibited Goods, Class II', or any other similar name:
(a) Items, kits, or modifications tools that can be used to modify a firearm;
(b) Crates containing illegal firearms;
(c) Crates containing illegal ammunition.
(d) Gavels; and
(e) Items which show membership, admittance or allegiance to a criminal organization or enterprise.
The following items shall collectively be known as ‘Prohibited Goods, Class III’, or any other similar name:
(a) Gold Bars;
(b) Silver Bars;
(c) Dirty Money;
(d) Encrypted Phone;
(e) Military Encryption Cards; and
(f) File of Military Intelligence.
(g) Underground Firearms Access Card.
(h) Lockpicks.

“Underground Firearms Access Card” shall refer to any physical or digital card, token, pass, code, or other medium designed, issued, or possessed for the primary purpose of granting or facilitating entry to any building, room, or premises where firearms, firearm parts, or firearm modification kits are offered, transferred, or sold in violation of the laws of the State of Mayflower. Possession of such a card shall be unlawful unless by a law-enforcement officer or other person acting under the authority of a law-enforcement agency in the course of official duties.

“Lockpick” shall refer to any device, tool, or instrument designed, adapted, or primarily used for the purpose of unlocking a lock without the use of the key or code intended by the lock’s manufacturer, except when possessed by a duly licensed locksmith, a person acting under the direction of a law-enforcement agency, or a person possessing such tools solely for lawful occupational, educational, or hobbyist purposes unrelated to any unlawful entry.
Any item within this section shall be known as Controlled Substance.
It shall be illegal for an individual to be in possession of:
(a) Nopyfruit, except when in its concentrated form;
(b) Jarniwanus, in any form; or
(c) Gushie, in any form.
The Department of Justice shall maintain a publicly accessible registry containing a list of Prohibited Goods and Controlled Substances found within this chapter.
Any person who is found in possession of an item which is a Prohibited Good, Class I shall be liable for arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 1702 "Possession of Prohibited Goods I."
Any person who is found in possession of an item which is a Prohibited Good, Class II shall be liable for citation or arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 1703 "Possession of Prohibited Goods II."
Any person who is found in possession of an item which is a Prohibited Good, Class III shall be liable for citation or arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 1704 "Possession of Prohibited Goods III."

Any person who is found in possession of an item which is a Controlled Substance which weighs up or equal to 15 weight units shall be liable for citation or arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 1706 "Petty Possession of Controlled Goods."

Any person who is found in possession of an item which is a Controlled Substance, which weighs between or equal to 16 and 30 weight units, shall be liable for citation or arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 1707 "Grand Possession of Controlled Goods."
Any person who is found in possession of a Controlled Substance in a weight greater or equal to 31 weight units shall be liable for arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 1708 "Felony Possession of Controlled Goods."
Gavels shall only be possessed by:
(a) The President of the Senate and their designated Senator(s).
(b) Justices and Judges of the State Judiciary.
“Criminal Organization” shall refer to any organization labelled placed on the Mayflower State Criminal Organization Registry by the Attorney General.

“Street Gang” shall refer to any organization with less than 30 (thirty) active members taking part in crimes against the State Code that do not require a conviction in order to issue prison sentences for.

“Senior Member” shall refer to any member of a Criminal Organization who holds a position of command in such an organization and is capable of directing subordinates to take part in organized criminal activity.

The Attorney General shall have the power to designate any organization as a Criminal Organization as he deems fit and appropriate, however such orders may be overturned by the Governor (with such overturns being open to counter-overturning by the Senate).

The Governor shall wield the power to revoke the residency of any senior member of a Criminal Organization, with the advice of the State Security Council and other such advisors with knowledge as to the capabilities and identities of senior criminals.
The Attorney General shall have the power to designate any organization as a Street Gang as he deems fit and appropriate.
The Attorney General shall maintain an up-to-date, publicly available database displaying information pertaining to Street Gangs, their operations and their known members.

The Governor shall wield the power to revoke the residency of any senior member of a Street Gang, with the advice of the State Security Council and other such advisors with knowledge as to the capabilities and identities of such Street Gang leaders.

records.text: A proprietary security guard shall be defined as an employee who is employed exclusively by any one employer whose primary duty is to provide security services for his or her employer, whose services are not contracted out to any other entity.

A proprietary private security employer shall be defined as a person who has one or more employees who provide security services for the employer and only the employer. A person who employs proprietary security guards pursuant to this definition at more than one location owned and operated by the employer shall still be considered a single employer

A security guard or security officer shall be defined as an employee of a private patrol operator who is licensed to and performs the duties of a private patrol operator in compliance with the provisions of this Chapter.

A private patrol operator and or any other variation thereof shall be defined as a person and or organization, who, for any consideration whatsoever; agrees to furnish, or furnishes a security officer or guard, or other person to protect persons or property to prevent the theft, loss, embezzlement, or concealment of any goods, merchandise, money, or property of any kind; or performs the service of a security officer or guard for any of these purposes.

The Department of State shall form a commission responsible for the enforcement of the provisions of this Chapter. Furthermore this commission shall be uniquely responsible for the issuance, suspension, and revocation of security licenses in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter.

records.text: Any individual seeking employment as a security officer employed by a private patrol operator, or wishing to incorporate or otherwise establish an organization defined as a private patrol operator shall be required to maintain an active security license from the Department of State.
(a) Proprietary security guards shall be required to maintain an active security license to carry a firearm while acting in the capacity of a proprietary security guard.

Previous to being issued a license the applicant shall complete a course of training in the exercise of the power of arrest, a course in the training of carrying and use of firearms, and the general use of force regarding specialized tools and equipment.

An individual representing the organization of which they are employed and acting in the capacity of a security officer or proprietary security guard shall be required to display a unique uniform compliant with this Chapter designated by their employer.
(a) For the purpose of this code, a uniform shall be considered compliant if it aligns with all of the following components:
(i) A uniform which bears at least one patch, badge, ID, logo, or otherwise emblem visible at all times clearly identifying the employing company.

(ii) Authorized officers may perform duties regulated under this chapter in 'non uniformed' status on a limited special assignment basis, and only when duty circumstances or special requirements of the client necessitate such dress. Licensees who are performing bodyguard or executive protection services may choose to carry their authorized equipment while in non uniformed status as needed in the conduct of such services.
(b) Security officers and or proprietary security guards which fail to comply with the uniform mandate shall not receive any protection or exemption by the provisions of this act.

A licensed private security officer or licensed proprietary security guard which has in their possession a valid firearms license shall be permitted to carry and display in public and/or in a restricted or otherwise firearms freezone, if the aforementioned restricted or otherwise firearms freezone is within the reasonable scope of their duties, a loaded firearm.

A licensed security officer shall be permitted to carry on their person and utilize, when on duty and conducting official security duties, and in accordance with provisions of State law the following articles of equipment and their respective ammunition or otherwise essential components; extendable, fixed and straight batons, stun guns or taser devices, pepper-spray or other similar chemical self-defense items, encrypted handheld radios, fixed or chain connected handcuffs; and the Bennetti 17 pistol.

A private security officer specifically directed to do so by an on-duty peace officer as defined by the State Code may be permitted to assist in the detainment, arrest, or capture of a criminal wrongdoer; however, security officers shall never, under any circumstances, be authorized to engage or assist directly or indirectly, in a vehicular pursuit. Private security officers may be permitted to close or block public roadways if authorized to do so by an on-duty supervisor of a law enforcement agency to ensure public safety during significant emergencies.

A security officer may only protect an asset, property or person when the security entity they are employed by has a contract or signed agreement to protect such asset, property or person and said security officer is authorized by his employer to provide such protective services.
For the purposes of this Subchapter, the term “authorized officer” shall be defined as a security officer, or proprietary security guard.

records.text: A fiscal period is a single month, starting on the first of the month and ending the last day of the month.
A fiscal quarter shall be defined as follows, with the quarter starting on the first day of the specified month and ending on the last day of the other specified month:
(a) Quarter 1: October to December.
(b) Quarter 2: January to March.
(c) Quarter 3: April to June.
(d) Quarter 4: July to September.
A fiscal year shall be defined as the 12-month period beginning 1 October and ending 30 September the following year.
References for fiscal years shall be made as “The [fiscal/financial] year of [the calendar year the fiscal year started in]”.

The term "commercial instrument" shall be defined to mean any document or item utilized in the course of commercial transactions or business operations that holds legal or financial significance that evidences, constitutes, or facilitates a business or financial transaction.
All Financial Statements that are required by law must meet requirements adopted by the Governor’s Office.
(a) The Governor shall be obligated to create a position within his office to accommodate this.
All businesses registered with the Department of State that offer stocks, bonds or investment contracts are obligated to prepare and publish the following financial statements every fiscal quarter:
(a) A Statement of Cash Flows
(b) A Balance Sheet
(c) Income Statement
All required Financial Statements must be made public within three (3) days of the end of each fiscal quarter.
All financial statements submitted to the SEC must be complete and accurate.

CASINO FINANCIALS. This chapter/Subchapter of the State Code is established to provide laws pertaining to the oversight, regulation, fairness, transparency, and accountability of Casino and Online Games websites and operations run within, or operating within, the State of Mayflower.

Businesses conducting gambling or casino like operations, herein “Casino” must be responsible for transparency with their financials, and shall be obligated to prepare and publicly announce the following Financial Statements every fiscal quarter:
(a) A Statement of Cash Flows.
(b) A Balance Sheet.
(c) Income Statement.
(d) Ledger of Cash Disbursements.
A Casino may not permit an individual user to withdraw more than $7,000,000 of their deposits/winnings at the casino in a 7 day period.

CONSUMER PROTECTIONS. Businesses conducting casino-like operations must be responsible for listing odds for all games. Whether it is in percentile or fraction format, the odds for all games. The odds must be displayed in a manner that a reasonable person would be able to properly read from a reasonable distance.
Casinos must disclose publicly and visibly any and all games in which the “house” or the business is favored to win the game, or in other words, where the person has a 49% chance or less to win.

Casinos must publicly report changes in odds, gameplay, or any other mechanic that may alter the experience of the casino in any way when the changes are made and in a monthly report. If there is no alteration as described above, a monthly report need not be published.
Any advertisement or promotion for Casinos must provide, in visible font and coloring that a reasonable person can see from a reasonable distance, a support website for chronic gambling addictions.
Should there be discrepancies or inaccuracies the Attorney General or District Attorney should direct an investigative agency to investigate the matter.
The Attorney General or District Attorney may take enforcement through civil and/or criminal court as prescribed by law.

Businesses that fail to comply with the prescribed Financial Reporting requirements will result in the business owner(s) being subject to various civil penalties as outlined by the Mayflower Tort Claims Act.
(a) This shall primarily fall under Negligent and Economic Torts but shall not be limited to such.

Businesses that fail to comply with the prescribed Financial Reporting requirements will result in the business owner(s) being subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1406 (Unlawful Operation of a Business) if—
(a) The business in question has been non-compliant with Financial Reporting requirements prescribed by law for a cumulative period of twenty one (30) days.
A new Chapter within the Mayflower Criminal Code shall be created: “Financial Crimes."
All crimes within Section IV of the Financial Reporting and Crimes Act shall be classified as Financial Crimes.
The following crimes shall be created and codified within the Mayflower Criminal Code:
“Bank Robbery” shall be created and defined as follows:
(a) Any person whether by force or intimidation, that takes any property or money in the care, custody, control, etc. of any bank, credit union, or savings and loan institution.
(b) Shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 30 minutes in prison.
(c) This statue shall be set to active within the Mayflower Criminal Code.
“Money Laundering” shall be created and defined as follows:

(a) Any person, knowing that the property involved in a financial transaction represents the proceeds of some form of unlawful activity, conducts or attempts to conduct such a financial transaction which in fact involves the proceeds of unlawful activity with the intent to promote the carrying on of specified unlawful activity; or knowing that the transaction is designed in whole or in part;
(i) to conceal or disguise the nature, the location, the source, the ownership, or the control of the proceeds of specified unlawful activity; or
(ii) to avoid a transaction reporting requirement under Local, State or Federal law;
(b) Shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 30 minutes in prison and/or face a fine of not more than $5,000 or twice the value of the property involved in the transaction, whichever is greater.
(c) This statue shall be set to active within the Mayflower Criminal Code.
“Embezzlement” shall be created and defined as follows:
(a) A person who shall, having lawful custody of property not his or her own, appropriate the same to his or her own use, with intent to deprive the owner thereof;
(b) Shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 50 minutes in prison and/or face a fine of not more than $5,000 or twice the value of the property involved in the transaction, whichever is greater.
(c) This statue shall be set to By Conviction within the Mayflower Criminal Code.
“Counterfeiting” shall be created and defined as follows:
(a) Any person, with intent to defraud, falsely makes, forges, counterfeits, or alters any obligation or other security of the State of Mayflower or Union of Columbia;
(b) Shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 120 minutes in prison.
(c) This statue shall be set to By Conviction within the Mayflower Criminal Code.
1 M.S.C. § 1301 “Bribery” shall be reclassified as a Financial Crime.

“Loan Sharking” shall be added and defined as follows: Any Lender who provides a loan not in accordance with Usury Laws or Loan Prohibitions shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 25 minutes in prison and/or face a fine of not more than $20,000 or twice the value of the loan, whichever is greater.

Commercial instrument falsification in the second degree’ shall be defined as follows: Any person who, with intent to defraud, knowingly falsifies, alters, or forges any commercial instrument shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
A “Borrower” shall be defined as a person or business who is loaned money from a Lender.
A “Lender” shall be defined as a business which loans money to a Borrower.

A “loan” shall be defined as a sum of money or other asset provided by a Lender to a Borrower under an agreement that it will be repaid in the future, typically with interest as compensation for the use of the funds.

An “interest rate” shall be defined as “the percentage charged or paid on the principal amount of a loan or deposit, calculated over a specified period, as agreed between the Lender and Borrower or deposit holder and institution.”
A “collateral” shall be defined as an asset or property offered by a Borrower to be given to the Lender should the Borrower fail to repay the loan.
This chapter may be cited as the "Loan Shark Extinction Act."
A Lender must have the loan readily available to the Borrower upon effect of the loan.
The Borrower must repay the loan and in full to the Lender by the conclusion of the loan.
A Lender may request collateral from a Borrower as a security against a loan.
(a) The collateral must be agreed in writing in the same document the loan is signed on.
(b) Should the Borrower fail to repay the loan, the collateral shall automatically be transferred to the ownership of the Lender.

A loan may only be offered by a Lender where the Borrower can repay the loan in whole, or at an agreed rate or repayment of weekly, fortnightly, monthly, once every two months, quarterly, once every 6 months, or yearly.
An interest rate may not be larger than:
(a) 40% of a principle where the loan rate of repayment is of weekly or fortnightly recurrence.
(b) 35% of a principle where the loan rate of repayment is monthly, once every two months, or quarterly.
(c) 30% of a principle where the loan rate of repayment is once every 6 months, or yearly.
A loan may not include:
(a) Hidden fees.
(b) Clauses that waive the rights of a Borrower.
(c) Clauses that unfairly benefit the Lender.
A Lender may not:
(a) Use methods of threats, coercion, harassment or intimidation to collect loan repayments.
(b) Offer a loan where the Borrower has no reasonable method to repay it.
Borrowers that fail to repay a loan as agreed by the Lender shall be liable to be subjected to various civil penalties as outlined by the Mayflower Tort Claims Act.
The Attorney General or District Attorney may take enforcement of Usury Laws through civil and/or criminal court as prescribed by law.

Lenders that fail to comply with the prescribed Usury Laws or Loan Prohibitions will result in the business owners being subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1606 “Loan Sharking”.
Lenders that use threats, coercion, harassment or intimidation to collect loan repayments shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 2308 “Extortion”.

The term “Insurance Policy” shall refer to an agreement between a Policyholder and Insurance Business where the Insurance Business agrees that they will payout a Policyholder as a result of a successful Claim.
The term “Policyholder” shall refer to a person or organization which is issued an insurance policy by an Insurance Business.
The term “Insurance Business” shall refer to a licensed business which provides insurance to a Policyholder.
The term “Claim” shall refer to when a Policyholder makes a request to the Insurance Business for compensation or coverage as dictated by an insurance policy.
The term “Premium” shall refer to the charge that a Policyholder receives from the Insurance Business to be covered by insurance, typically at a recurring rate.

(a) Have a minimum capital of the result of the following formula:

(b) Provide the Commerce Office a prospective business report that includes, in the order as listed:
