The Commerce Office must deny any application to be a licensed Insurance Business where:
(a) The Insurance Business owner has been charged with any crime listed under Subtitle 1, Chapter IV of the Mayflower Criminal Code.
(b) The Insurance Business owner has been charged with any crime listed under Subtitle 1, Chapter VI of the Mayflower Criminal Code.
(c) The Insurance Business owner has been charged with any crime listed under Subtitle 5 of the Mayflower State Code.
(d) The Insurance Business owner has failed to properly file a prospective business report.

Insurance Businesses must clearly outline all types of Insurance Policies and its individual rules provided by the Insurance Business in a clear and discernable method, which is publicly accessible, which includes:
(a) How the Insurance Policy applies to the Policyholder;
(b) The Premium of the Insurance Policy;
(c) The term of coverage that the Policyholder receives for the Insurance Policy; and
(d) An example on how the Insurance Policy will compensate the Policyholder.
Every month, if a Policyholder submits a Claim to the Insurance Business, the Insurance Business must publish a summary claims report which is publicly accessible that includes:
(a) The total amount of Claims submitted by Policyholders;
(b) The total amount of Claims accepted by the Insurance Business;
(c) The total amount of Claims rejected by the Insurance Business, with their reason(s) for rejection;
(d) The total amount of Policyholders, including the difference from the previous public report;
(e) Any changes to an Insurance Policy;
(f) Any loans that the Insurance Business has obtained to finance the Insurance Business, and the amount of money the loan is worth;
(g) Any court convictions against the Insurance Business;
(h) Any commercial punishments against the Insurance Business by the Commerce Office; and
(i) A link to the prospective business report.
Every six months an Insurance Business must submit a summary claims report, regardless if a Claim was submitted by a Policyholder that month.
An Insurance Business may not:
(a) Use methods of threats, coercion, harassment or intimidation to collect a premium; and
(b) Offer an Insurance Policy where the Policyholder has no reasonable method to repay it.
An Insurance Business may only change the rules of an Insurance Policy every 30 days.
Such a change must be publicly announced seven days before the change comes into effect.

Should the premium of an Insurance Policy be changed, a Policyholder who is already covered by the Insurance Policy shall not have their premium affected for more or less until they are required to pay their Premium again.
An Insurance Policy may not include:
(a) Hidden fees;
(b) Clauses that waive the right of the Policyholder; and
(c) Clauses that unfairly benefit the Lender.
A premium may not be more than:
(a) 10% of the maximum Claim if the premium is paid at an increment of time that is monthly, or shorter; or
(b) 15% of the maximum Claim if the premium is paid at an increment of time that is longer than monthly.
A Policyholder may not fraudulently submit a Claim to an Insurance Business.
There may not be a “cooldown” period for submitting a Claim.
An Insurance Business may only reject to compensate for a Claim submitted by a Policyholder where:
(a) The Policyholder misrepresents the facts in a Claim;
(b) The Policyholder fails to pay Premiums;
(c) The Policyholder requests the Claim as a result of their involvement in criminal activity;
(d) The Policyholder attempts to submit a Claim for something that is not covered by the Insurance Policy;
Such a denial must be outlined in writing, with reference to the relevant statute.
An Insurance Business must submit to quarterly financial inspections by the Commerce Office and/or the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation.

During such times, the Insurance Business must make all documents related to the operation of the Insurance Business available to the Commerce Office and/or Mayflower Bureau of Investigation upon request.
An Insurance Business which intends to shutdown, which is not a result of financial issues, must:
(a) Notify the Commerce Office seven days before shutting down.
(b) Notify Policyholders fourteen days before shutting down.
(c) Refuse to accept new Policyholders within fourteen days of shutting down.
(d) Refuse to collect any Premiums within seven days of shutting down.
(e) Publicly publish a statement of cash flows.
(f) Publicly publish a balance sheet.
(g) Publicly publish a summary claims report.
An Insurance Business which intends to shutdown, which is a result of financial issues, must—
(a) Attempt to rectify the issue by:
(i) Raising the required capital.

(ii) Submitting a new prospective business report which has a reduced maximum Claim amount, and/or maximum Policyholders amount which is not smaller than the amount of Policyholders that are currently on an Insurance Policy.
(iii) Refuse to accept new Policyholders.
(iv) Notifying the Commerce Office.
(b) Conduct the following actions if they fail to rectify the issue:
(i) Notify the Commerce Office seven days before shutting down.
(ii) Notify Policyholders seven days before shutting down.
(iii) Refuse to accept new Policyholders within seven days of shutting down.
(iv) Refuse to collect any Premiums within seven days of shutting down.
(v) Pay outstanding Claims.
(vi) Publicly publish a statement of cash flows.
(vii) Publicly publish a balance sheet.
(viii) Publicly publish a summary claims report.
(ix) Turn over all financial documents to the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation.
If a business owner who no longer meets the requirements prescribed by the Commerce Office to legally own a business, is the owner of an Insurance Business, then:
(a) The ownership of the Insurance Business shall automatically be transferred to the Secretary of State.
(b) The original business owner must transfer the capital of the Insurance Business to the Secretary of State.
(i) The Department of Justice may direct law enforcement to seize assets owned by the original owner and sell them off to recuperate the capital.
(c) The Commerce Office must find a new owner for the business.
(i) The Commerce Office may sell the ownership in whole or in portions.
(d) The Commerce Office must cease the operations of the business until the new owner(s) are decided.
“Insurance Claims Misconduct” shall be defined as:
(a) Any Insurance Business that rejects a Claim by an Policyholder for a reason not outlined in Section VI, or fails to publish a summary claims report where required.
(b) Shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 30 minutes in prison, and/or face a fine of not more than $40,000 or three times the value of the Premium, whichever is greater.
“Insurance Fraud” shall be defined as:
(a) Any Policyholder that fraudulently submits a Claim to an Insurance Business;
(b) Shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 25 minutes in prison, and/or face a fine of not more than $30,000 or four times the value of the Claim, whichever is greater.

Insurance Businesses that offer Insurance Policies to more than the maximum number of Policyholders as outlined in the prospective business report shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1406 “Unlawful Operation of a Business”.

Insurance Businesses that offer Claims that are larger than the maximum Claim outlined in the prospective business report shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1406 “Unlawful Operation of a Business”.

Insurance Businesses that do not have the minimum capital required to operate the Insurance Business shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1406 “Unlawful Operation of a Business”.
Insurance Businesses that improperly reject a Claim shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1410 "Insurance Claims Misconduct”.
Insurance Businesses that fail to publish a summary claims report when required shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1406 “Unlawful Operation of a Business”.
Insurance Businesses that use threats, coercion, harassment or intimidation to collect a Premium shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 2308 “Extortion”.
Policyholders that fraudulently submits a Claim to an Insurance Business shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 3108 “Insurance Fraud”.

Policyholders that fail to pay a Premium as agreed by the Insurance Business and the Policyholder shall be liable to be subjected to various civil penalties as outlined by the Mayflower Tort Claims Act.

Insurance Businesses that fail to pay an approved Claims as permitted by the Comprehensive Insurance Act shall be liable to be subjected to various civil penalties as outlined by the Mayflower Tort Claims Act.

“Transportation Service Company” or “TSC” shall refer to any business registered with the State Department whose primary service is to offer transportation through the means of employing taxi operators or other private drivers.
“Incorporated Private Driver” or “IPD” shall refer to any individual employed by a Transportation Service Company as a taxi/transportation operator .

“Unincorporated Private Driver” or “UPD” shall refer to any individual that carries out transportation services using their own private vehicle and is not employed by or affiliated with any Transportation Service Company.

“Fare” shall refer to an amount of U.C. Dollars agreed between a private vehicle operator and customer, to be paid to the vehicle operator either before or after successful completion of the requested journey.
Transportation Service Companies shall be required to maintain a publicly accessible database of their drivers, including but not limited to the following:
(a) the driver's Roblox username;
(b) the driver's date of hire;
(c) the driver's position;
(d) the driver's registered vehicle model; and
(e) the license plate of the driver's registered vehicle model.
Transportation Service Companies shall only hire drivers that possess a Mayflower Driving License.

Transportation Service Companies shall be required to temporarily suspend the employment of drivers that have had their Mayflower Driving License revoked, until the repossession of the license by the driver.

Transportation Service Companies shall be obligated to implement policy that details potential administrative action against employees who in any instance have met all of either sections of the following criteria:
(a) the employee had a passenger in the vehicle;
(b) the employee drove recklessly and in a manner that endangered other drivers and pedestrians; or
(c) the employee was arrested for a Misdemeanour or Felony against the Mayflower Vehicle Code, whilst in the commission of his transportation service vehicle.

The liability of Transportation Service Companies over their employees shall depend on the type of business (as detailed and regulated by the Department of State) however TSCs that are not already liable for their employees shall be required to provide legal counsel and/or sufficient legal advice to drivers facing civil suits for actions committed whilst in the operation of their transportation service vehicle [provided that they are on-duty and representing the TSC employed by].
Unincorporated Private Drivers are required to possess a Mayflower Driving License whilst offering their transportation services to the public.

Unincorporated Private Drivers shall temporarily suspend their offering of transportation services to the public, should they have their Mayflower Driving License revoked, however the suspension may be self-lifted once they have repossessed their license.
Unincorporated Private Drivers shall be completely liable for their own actions.

If a UPD becomes employed by a TSC and becomes an IPD, the TSC shall not be required to provide legal counsel or advice if the driver is facing a civil suit regarding actions committed before their employment, whilst they were in a UPD capacity.

This subchapter shall apply to all private drivers offering transportation services, whether incorporated or unincorporated. This section shall not apply to private drivers with overriding contracts with individuals that detail a contractually agreed pay rate (e.g., Personal Limousine Drivers).
All drivers shall be required to charge a minimum fare of $50 (fifty dollars) per ride request.
All drivers must be informed [by the customer] of the location that the customer wishes to be driven to, before the passenger enters the transportation service vehicle.
All drivers shall be required to make the total fare of the requested journey aware to the customer, before embarking on the journey.
All drivers must detail whether the customer is to pay the fare before or after successful completion of the journey.
A driver may only embark on the requested journey once a price and timing of payment has been agreed between the driver and the customer.
The term “Security” shall refer to a stock, bond, or investment contract.
The term “Stock Issuer” shall refer to any person or business that issues a security.
The term “Exchange” shall refer to any organized platform which is a place for buying or selling securities.
Any Security must be registered with the Department of State in a method deemed acceptable by the Secretary of State.

It shall be prohibited to buy or sell a security while in possession of non-public price-sensitive information about the security, or tip off another individual about the non-public price-sensitive information who then buys or sells the security.
(a) Any individual that infringes on this provision shall be liable for criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1607 “Insider Trading.”
(b) They shall be liable for a citation for $50,000 or three times the worth of the security traded or attempted to be traded, whichever is greater.
It shall be prohibited to misrepresent or omit key facts of a business or security to investors.
(a) Any individual that infringes on this provision shall be liable for criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1608 “Securities Fraud."
(b) They shall be liable for a citation for $80,000 or four times the worth of the security traded or attempted to be traded, whichever is greater.
It shall be prohibited to falsely portray a business to have a security which is actively being bought or sold.
(a) Any individual that infringes on this provision shall be liable for criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1609 “Market Manipulation.”
(b) They shall be liable for a citation for $70,000 or four times the worth of the security traded or attempted to be traded, whichever is greater.
Any changes to the cost of a security must be logged in an accessible and publicly viewable manner by both the Exchange and Stock Issuer.
(a) Any individual that infringes on this provision shall be liable for criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1608 “Securities Fraud.
(b) They shall be liable for a citation for $80,000 or four times the worth of the security traded or attempted to be traded, whichever is greater.
It shall be unlawful for an individual without a bar certification to represent another individual in a legal proceeding unless they are supervised by a bar certified individual.
(a) Any individual who infringes on this provision shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1510 “Fraudulent Practice of Law” and liable for up to 60 minutes in prison, a citation up to $45,000, or both.

(b) Where the individual has charged a client for their service, the infringing individual shall be further liable for up to a 120 in prison, a citation up to the greater amount of either $60,000 or four times the amount charged, or both.
It shall be unlawful to advertise an individual as an attorney or as having an active bar certification where that individual does not have an active bar certification.
(a) Any individual who infringes on this provision shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1510 “Fraudulent Practice of Law” and liable for up to 60 minutes in prison, a citation up to $45,000, or both.
All actions listed in this Chapter shall be considered an administrative action.

records.text: Demotion shall be considered the involuntary reduction of rank or grade.
(a) Transferring into a different unit and taking a reduction in rank shall be considered a voluntary action if the person knew that such reduction was a prerequisite for their transfer.
It is unlawful to arbitrarily, or without due observance of law, demote someone from a non-staff position.
A voluntary general discharge may be issued upon request for resignation by an employee.
(a) For the purposes of this section, a voluntary general discharge is not an administrative action.

(b) Whether or not to give a voluntary general discharge or honorable discharge is up to the due discretion of the agency so long as they prescribe concrete rules and regulations to the degree each set of circumstances warrant.
An involuntary general discharge may be issued to a conditional employee, or to a non-conditional employee following—
(a) an internal affairs investigation, where—
(i) that investigation found wrongdoing; and
(ii) that the wrongdoing was in the form of negligence or recklessness;
(b) an employee’s failure to uphold mandated activity standards—without approved leave—defined within department policy in the form of Activity Check(s) and/or the submission of an Activity Log(s).
It is unlawful to arbitrarily, or without due observance of law, to issue an involuntary general discharge to a non-conditional employee.
Voluntary general discharges may not be reviewed by any administrative court or court of law or court of equity.
Involuntary general discharges issued to conditional employees may not be reviewed by any court.

“Activity check” shall be defined as a review used to measure employee activity where the employee is required to sign a document or form. The employee must be allotted at least 72 hours to complete this form or document.

“Activity log” shall be defined as the act of clocking in/out while performing duties related to a specific department or otherwise measuring contributions and/or completion of duties assigned to an employee
A dishonorable discharge shall serve as a bar of employment from the issuing agency for at most four (4) months after its issuance.
A dishonorable discharge may be issued only following an internal affairs investigation and–
(a) the investigation found wrongdoing; and
(b) a finding of wanton disregard for policy, statute, or regulation; or
(c) a finding of an intentional act.
It is unlawful to arbitrarily, or without due observance of law, issue a dishonorable discharge.
A dishonorable discharge shall not be reviewed by any administrative court or court of law unless—
(a) there is clear and present factual error in the issuance of the dishonorable discharge; or
(b) the dishonorable discharge was plainly and clearly arbitrary or its defined offense is ambiguous.
(c) the action is unconstitutional.

An administrative demerit shall be any system colloquially referred to as a “strike” or “warning.” Furthermore, such a system, upon receipt of a “strike,” demerit or “warning;” will place a disability upon its recipient or place them in jeopardy of a disability or administrative action.
An administrative demerit need not be issued by an internal investigation unit.
An administrative demerit shall not be reviewed by any administrative court or court of law unless—
(a) there is clear and present factual error in the issuance of the demerit; or
(b) the demerit was plainly and clearly arbitrary or its defined offense is ambiguous.
It is unlawful to arbitrarily, or without due observance of law, issue an administrative demerit.
A prejudicial transfer shall be a forced transfer of one person to another unit or division without their consent.
A prejudicial transfer may be issued upon any case and at any time unless—
(a) the transfer was retaliatory;
(b) the transfer was discriminatory; or
(c) the transfer was a result of a personal gripe, vendetta, or severe conflict.
A prejudicial transfer may only be reviewed by an administrative court in circumstances of 4 M.S.C. 7 §§ 1502(a)-1502(c).
(a) The complainant must prove more likely than not that the transfer violated 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1502.
Suspension shall refer to the prevention of a person from executing their duties and collecting pay for either a set period of time or indefinitely.

Administrative leave shall be the indefinite suspension pending an investigation. A person may only be put on administrative leave for allegations which, if taken as true, would warrant a general discharge or dishonorable discharge.

(a) A person may only be on administrative leave for no longer than ten (10) days; however, a person may be put on administrative leave for longer if there is a criminal investigation supplemented by order from the Department of Justice for the person to be placed on administrative leave.
(b) Administrative leave may be used in extreme cases where the probable punishment of suspension – however, the length of suspension must have the days on administrative leave subtracted from it.
(c) Administrative leave may only be used if there is a pending misconduct investigation or criminal investigation.

(d) Any administrative leave imposed as a result of a pending misconduct investigation or criminal investigation shall last up to thirty (30) days or until the conclusion of the investigation, whichever occurs first.

(i) If, upon conclusion of a misconduct or criminal investigation, probable cause of a criminal violation is found and the matter is pending review for criminal charges by the Department of Justice, the administrative leave imposed under 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d) may be extended for a period not to exceed seven (7) additional days. Such extension shall not be subject to the thirty (30) day limit prescribed in 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d).

(e) Any administrative leave extended pursuant to 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d)(i) may be further extended for an indefinite period if, during the seven (7) day extension, criminal charges are formally filed. In such cases, administrative leave shall continue until the conclusion of the subsequent criminal matter.
There shall be no review by an administrative court of the placement of someone on administrative leave unless—
(a) the placement was not by an internal affairs entity, command entity;
(b) the suspension has gone on longer than allowed under 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(a); or

(c) the administrative leave extended under 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d), 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d)(i), or 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(e) exceeds its respective limitations without criminal filing or conclusion of the investigation.
Involuntary suspension shall refer to a suspension as specified in 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1601 for a period of time no longer than seven (7) days.
A person may be suspended for a violation of the policy, rule, or procedure notwithstanding the existence of or there the results of an internal investigation for no longer than three (3) days.
A person may only be suspended for greater than three (3) days upon recommendation and finding of fact from a bona fide misconduct investigation.
It is unlawful to arbitrarily, or without due observance of law, issue a suspension demerit.
The Attorney General shall serve as the designated enforcer of 4 M.S.C. 7 §§ 1602(d), 1602(d)(i), 1602(e), 1603(a), 1603(b), and 1603(c).

Any department, agency, or official in violation of the procedures prescribed in either 4 M.S.C. 7 §§ 1602(d), 1602(d)(i), 1602(e), 1603(a), 1603(b), or 1603(c) may be subject to administrative or civil action under 4 M.S.C. 7 § 2601 et seq.

Individuals subjected to administrative leave beyond the timelines established herein, without statutory justification or a proper extension, may file an administrative claim pursuant to 4 M.S.C. 7 § 3402.
It shall be unlawful to arbitrarily, or without due observance of law, issue a blacklist.
Arbitrary punishment is defined as:
(a) punishment that has no backing in regulation, policy, or law;
(b) punishment whose policy, law, or regulation prescribing it is ambiguous, or unclear, or a violation of a constitutional right or privilege or statutory enactment;
(c) punishment with no factual backing;
(d) punishment outside and beyond what is explicitly prescribed in policy; or
(e) punishment that takes no accounting of mitigating factors, circumstances, or liabilities.
Arbitrary punishment is prohibited.
A primary agency shall be any as so defined:
(a) The Mayflower State Police.
(b) Any county law enforcement agency.
(c) Any municipal law enforcement agency.
A secondary agency shall be any as so defined:
(a) The Mayflower Transportation Authority.
(b) The Mayflower Parks and Wildlife Department.
(c) Any fire department.
(d) Any railroad police department.
(e) The Mayflower Bureau of Investigation.
(f) The Mayflower Transportation Police.
(g) Any port authority police department.
An auxiliary agency shall be any as so defined:
(a) The Mayflower District Courts.
(b) The Department of Justice.
(c) The Office of the Governor.
(d) The Mayflower Supreme Court.
(e) Department of State.
(f) The State Senate.
(g) Any port authority, but does not include a port authority police department.
(h) Any law enforcement training institute.
(i) The Mayflower Public Broadcasting Service.
(j) The Mayflower Department of Transportation, including any subordinate agencies, but does not include the Mayflower Transportation Authority or the Mayflower Transportation Police.
(k) The Mayflower National Guard.
The rank at which a staff position begins shall be clearly defined by a department through their policy.

records.text: The principles of the merit system shall be as follows:

(a) Recruitment should be from qualified individuals from appropriate sources in an endeavor to achieve a work force from all segments of society, and selection and advancement should be determined solely on the basis of relative ability, knowledge and skills, after fair and open competition which assures that all receive equal opportunity.

(b) All employees and applicants for employment should receive fair and equitable treatment in all aspects of personnel management without regard to political affiliation, race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, or handicapping condition, and with proper regard for their privacy and constitutional rights.
(c) All employees should maintain high standards of integrity, conduct, and concern for the public interest.
(d) The State workforce should be used efficiently and effectively.

(e) Employees should be retained on the basis of adequacy of their performance, inadequate performance should be corrected, and employees should be separated who cannot or will not improve their performance to meet required standards.
(f) Employees should be provided effective education and training in cases in which such education and training would result in better organizational and individual performance.
(g) Employees should be—
(i) protected against arbitrary action, personal favoritism, or coercion for political purposes; and
(ii) prohibited from using their official authority or influence for the purpose of interfering with or affecting the result of an election or a nomination for election.

Employees should be protected against reprisal for the lawful disclosure of information which the employees reasonably believe evidences-- a violation of any law, rule, or regulation, or mismanagement, a gross waste of resources, an abuse of authority, or a substantial and specific danger to public safety.
The attributes of the merit system shall be as follows:
(a) When making decisions of employment or promotion, officials shall review the following attributes of merit:
(i) logged patrol/work hours for the current cycle;
(ii) past performance in other departments;
(iii) abilities to work as a team and play well with others, which is affirmed by testimony of another leader or employee;
(iv) demonstration of sound judgment, which is affirmed by testimony of another leader;
(v) demonstration of leadership qualities while holding a position in the State of Mayflower, which is affirmed by testimony of another leader or employee;
(vi) effort in the completion of an application, cover letter, or letter of interest;
(vii) scores on an accredited exam, if applicable;
(viii) commendations or written letters of recommendation; and
(ix) holding a valid accreditation, which may be required for the position.
(x) Completion of formal state training or continued education relevant to the position.
Performance in another community or group shall not be used as a means to demonstrate the merit of an individual.
When making a hiring decision officials can use the following attributes to discredit and demerit a hire:
(a) bad performance in another department or agency;
(b) poor completion of an application, cover letter, or letter of interest;
(c) poor accredited exam scores;
(d) past disciplinary actions;
(e) character defects which would bring harm to the health of the department or community;
(f) failure to use discretion;
(g) inability to gain a security clearance, other than not requiring it in the first place;
(h) refusal to comply with regulations or lawful orders;
(i) terrible activity in a previous department or agency; or
(j) no, or little experience within the State of Mayflower.
During the hiring process, an agency shall indicate all attributes of merit and demerit and subjectively, according to their own principles, weigh each application.
A competitive hiring round shall be any hiring period where the number of spots to be taken in is clearly defined, publicly posted, and limited.
(a) A department may not intake more than the number of applicants they have posted in a competitive hiring round.
A non-competitive hiring round shall be any hiring round where the number of spots is not clearly defined, publicly posted, and not limited.

(a) If a person passes all preceding stages in a non-competitive hiring round, then they must be accepted as their outcome so long as this would not cause the department to exceed their allocated budget.
An application / character screening may only be denied for an attribute of demerit, and accepted for an attribute of merit. If they have neither then they shall be denied.
No individual may skip more than three (3) consecutive ranks from their current rank.
(a) If any Department is found promoting someone over three (3) ranks, the Department of Justice shall investigate such Department for any findings of Nepotism and any level of Misconduct.
(b) The Mayflower National Guard shall be exempt from paragraph 2510 of this subchapter.

Complaints about a department violating the principles of the merit system shall be directed to the Governor, who shall in all cases, investigate and adjudicate violations of these claims. The Governor may delegate this responsibility to any persons employed by the Office of the Governor or the Department of Justice as he sees fit.
(a) The Governor may seek a written legal opinion from the Attorney General as to the legality of the violations.
The Governor, under a finding of intentional deprivation of an employment right, or failure to follow a merits-system practice, may request the Attorney General to begin legal proceedings.
The Attorney General may also, on his own accord, begin legal proceedings on any reasonable suspicion of violation.
(a) Such legal proceeding will take form in a civil action in the name of the State against the Department and any individuals within said Department violating the principles of the merit system.

If a complaint is substantiated and found to be more-likely than not in proving the existence of a violation, then the Governor shall remedy the complainant appropriately with respect to the offending agency.
Background checks shall be over an objective criteria that shall remain static and non-subjective.
Activity in other communities, games, or organizations shall not be evaluated in a background check unless:
(a) the activity was unlawful [in real life];
(b) the activity was extremely toxic; or
(c) the activity constitutes harassment or unlawful badgering.
Departments shall background check applicants and new-hires on the following criteria:
(a) Likelihood that the individual is an alternate account; which shall be evaluated under reasonableness.
(b) Whether the individual has their inventory open.
(c) Whether the individual is involved with a criminal or terrorist organization which has been declared by the Attorney General.
(d) Whether the individual has a certain amount of records that exceed a threshold.
(e) Whether the individual has a criminal conviction.
(f) A dishonorable discharge from the department, or other departments.
(g) Severe Moderation action against them with the exception of appealed Moderation action.
(h) Extremely toxic behavior, unlawful activities [in real life] or harassment in other communities, games, or organizations.
(i) Whether the individual is not a resident within the state.
(j) Whether the individual defects would bring harm to the health of the department.
(k) Whether the individual has past disciplinary actions taken against them within the last two (2) months in a department in which they are currently or were previously employed in.
If a department denies an individual due to them having their inventory hidden then they shall specify such on their results tracker.
(a) If a department denies an individual due to them failing their background check then they shall specify the reason on their results tracker.

Civil service agencies, the Mayflower Transportation Authority, or any fire department may enlist the services of any county law enforcement agency or the Mayflower State Police to perform background checks on their current or potential staff and personnel.

(a) The State Legislature may request that the Mayflower State Police conduct a background check on any nominee brought before them and be provided an unabridged report in which the Mayflower State Police shall conduct.
A prejudicial or unfair hiring practice is a hiring practice that does not conform to what has been established by law.

The term of an administrative court judge is for the duration of their term as a district court judge, unless the judge was appointed by the Governor whereso the term is three (3) months.

records.text: The administrative courts shall have the power to grant equitable remedy as necessary to ensure proper enforcement of law;
The administrative courts may not award damages in any case.
The administrative courts may not order the termination, discharge, or removal of another person, unless explicitly commanded to by law.
The administrative court may issue declaratory relief when necessary.
Administrative hearings have the following attributes:
(a) An administrative hearing may be called by any administrative court judge as remedy; or by an agency command member to review the factual basis of a claim.

(b) An administrative hearing shall be overseen by a tribunal which shall consist of two officers chosen by the department command, which may also be themselves; and an administrative court judge who shall preside.
(c) All claims of law shall be solely decided by the administrative court judge.
(d) All claims of fact shall be decided by the tribunal-at-large.

(e) The tribunal may recommend punitive action and to what degree. The command member who called the tribunal shall be able to reject or alter the action, however he may not increase it to a greater degree than what was recommended.
(f) All matters of the admittance of evidence or witnesses shall be solely decided by the presiding judge.
(g) The procedure for an administrative hearing shall be:
(i) Call to order by the presiding judge.
(ii) The presiding judge shall state the claims being made against him and present the claims in full.
(iii) The accused will be given a chance to introduce evidence of his own, and call witnesses as necessary.
(h) The accused will then be able to give a closing statement.
(i) The presiding judge shall adjourn the hearing.
Administrative claims have the following attributes:
(a) An administrative claim is a claim of law and not a claim of fact that an action was arbitrary or without due observance of law.
(b) Administrative claims shall be heard and decided only by an administrative court judge.
(c) As a result of an administrative claim, a judge may use all remedies afforded to him by law.
(d) The Supreme Court shall provide for the process, through rule, as to how an administrative claim be made and heard by an administrative court.
All relevant evidence, unless it violates another rule, shall be admitted.

records.text: The term "conditional employment" means:
(a) Employment that may be terminated at any point for any reason.

An employee shall be considered conditionally employed with a department from time of hire until which point they have successfully completed the requirements to become a full-time employee, as defined by department policy.
An employee shall be considered non-conditionally employed with a department after they have successfully completed the requirements to become a full-time employee, as defined by department policy.
An employee shall be considered conditional for no more than one month past their initial hire date.

Administrative action issued to a conditional employee maynot be reviewed by any administrative court, court of law, or court of equity. This shall not apply to a discharge of the conditional employee if one of the following are true:
(a) there is clear and present factual error in the issuance of the discharge; or
(b) the discharge was clearly retaliatory.

records.text: SHORT TITLE. This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Protect The Capitol Act.”
DEFINITIONS. For the purposes of this chapter, the term “Mayflower State Police” shall refer to the States law enforcement agency that resides within the State of Mayflower.
The term “State Capitol Building” shall refer to any publicly owned building which the State Senate convenes for legislative business.

The term “Grounds of the State Capitol” shall refer to any publicly owned property where the State Capitol Building is situated, including public walkways and roadways directly surrounding the property.

records.text: Public travel in, and occupancy of, the Grounds of the State Capitol is restricted to the sidewalks and other paved surfaces.
It is unlawful and punishable by 1 M.S.C. § 1507 “Unlawful Conduct in a Protected Building” to:
(a) To offer or expose any article for sale in the Grounds of the State Capitol.
(b) To display a sign, placard, or other form of advertisement in the Grounds of the State Capitol.
(c) To solicit fares, alms, subscriptions, or contributions in the Grounds of the State Capitol.

(d) Parade, stand, or move in processions or assemblages in the Grounds of the State Capitol, or to display in the Grounds of the State Capitol a flag, banner, garment or device designed or adapted to bring into public notice a party, organization, or movement.
The Grounds of the State Capitol shall be a Firearm Free Zone and Melee Free Zone.
There shall be a Congressional Park, which shall be situated within the parkland east of the State Capitol.
(a) It shall be permitted to walk on non-paved surfaces within the Congressional Park.
(b) It shall be forbidden to swim within the lake situated within the Congressional Parks, which shall be known as Bear Memorial Lake.

(c) The Congressional Parks shall be considered as extensions of the Grounds of the State Capitol, but not the roads or pathways directly surrounding it which are not part of the dedicated Grounds of the State Capitol.
There shall be a State Memorial Grounds, which shall be situated within the graveyard east of the Congressional Parks.
(a) It shall be permitted to walk on non-paved surfaces within the State Memorial Grounds.

(b) The State Memorial Grounds shall be considered as extensions of the Grounds of the State Capitol, but not the roads or pathways directly surrounding it which are not part of the dedicated Grounds of the State Capitol.
“Deadly force” shall refer to force that is intended or likely to cause death or serious bodily injury.

“Military installation” shall refer to any base, armory, depot, range, or facility operated by the Mayflower National Guard.
“Line-of-sight” shall refer to unobstructed visual range from a military installation’s outer perimeter.
